newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: US views attack on Taiwan with concern.
newsitem.headline: US views attack on Taiwan with concern.

text.p: Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said any attack on Taiwan by China would be a matter of "grave concern" for the United States.

But Albright, on a visit to the United Nations, sidestepped a query on whether she agreed with U.S. House of Representatives speaker Newt Gingrich's warning to China's top leaders that Washington would intervene militarily if Taiwan were attacked.

"We have always said that first of all that we have one China policy, second that we would like the issues between Taiwan and China to be worked out peacefully, that the security of Taiwan is of great importance to the United States and if there were any force used by the Chinese that is a matter of grave concern to the United States," Albright said.

Gingrich, after a three-day trip to China, said he had made it absolutely clear how the United States would respond if such a military conflict arose. "We want you to understand, we will defend Taiwan," he said.
The United States ended its official recognition of Taiwan when it re-established diplomatic relations with China two decades ago, but maintains unofficial ties with Taipai.

Albright was at the United Nations to discuss a variety of issues with U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan, including the Middle East, Zaire, Angola, the post of a new U.N. Human Rights Commissioner and U.N. reforms, according to U.N. officials. She also briefed him on the recent U.S.-Russia summit between Presidents Bill Clinton and Boris Yeltsin.
